eligibility.definition: str/int/float/bool fields only; exact types; no subclasses; ints within i64; no missing keys; no field carrying a user encoder or validator.
excluded_by_design: temporal kinds (date/datetime/time): the prototype's chrono parsing does not reproduce Python's temporal variants, so those fields are ineligible rather than handled wrongly
Decimal, UUID, containers, unions, nested models
int values outside i64: ineligible, never truncated
subclass instances, including bool where int is expected
missing keys (presence/default handling is not implemented)

fallback.note: A fallback costs the native attempt PLUS the full Python path. It is additive, never a substitute, so a workload with a high fallback rate is strictly worse off than pure Cython.

headline: RETAIN CYTHON. The sequential native executor is NOT promotion-eligible, on two independent grounds, either of which is sufficient. (1) COVERAGE: it can run ZERO of the 15 acceptance workloads -- every corpus model carries Decimal, UUID, temporal or container fields, all of which it declines by design. (2) ECONOMICS: crossing the Python/Rust boundary costs 1163 ns, which is 7.8% of a 15058 ns construction, while the ENTIRE saving the Cython gate delivered was about 9.9%. Native must spend most of the prize just to collect it, leaving roughly 2.1% of theoretical headroom against AC8's required 10% ADDITIONAL improvement. This is a completed negative experiment with measurements, not an unfinished build.

measurements.WARNING_about_the_optimistic_ratio: `ratio_point_estimate` compares an optimistic native path against a real Cython construction. The native side omits conversion, defaults, aliases, assignment and hooks, so the difference is dominated by work that was SKIPPED, not by validation made faster. It is reported as an upper bound and must not be quoted as an improvement.
measurements.native_side_is_optimistic: The native path skips conversion, defaults, aliases and hooks entirely (object.__new__ plus a dict update). It is an UPPER BOUND on the native design, not an achievable implementation.
measurements.plan_reuse: warm loops reuse one plan; creation is measured separately and is NOT amortised into the warm figures

protocol.note: Paired processes with alternating order, as the acceptance protocol requires -- not a single in-process scalar microbenchmark.

parity.note: Zero mismatches on the declared eligible subset. Parity holds; it is simply not enough to justify promotion.

why_not: Coverage: 0 of 15 acceptance workloads are eligible, so there is no declared eligible workload in the corpus on which a 10% additional improvement could even be demonstrated.
Economics: the unavoidable boundary floor is 7.8% of a construction against a total available saving of roughly 9.9%.
Parity is fine, but parity is a precondition for promotion, not a reason for it.

reproduce: python -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'.'); from benchmarks.native_validation import full_cost_comparison; print(full_cost_comparison())"
retained: The frozen optimized Cython artifact from TASK-16 remains the implementation. No production Cython or Rust source was changed by this task, and no default backend was installed.
what_would_change_the_answer: Native coverage of Decimal, UUID and temporal types with exact Python semantics -- which is where the real corpus cost lives, and which the prototype deliberately declines because its chrono handling does not reproduce Python's temporal variants.
A boundary cheap enough to leave headroom: today it consumes most of the available saving before any validation is performed.
A workload dominated by validation rather than conversion/assignment/hooks. The Cython gate already removed the generic dispatch, so what remains is mostly NOT validation.
